findings.closure: Deduplicated pull batches only move the cursor forward; a failed recovery stays scheduled and is retried by the timer instead of being lost.
Persisted usage is added to the locally recorded delta with an upper bound so a newer persisted value is not double counted; pending calls can no longer be hidden by a non-zero persisted baseline.
Legacy nested entries resolve their parent only within the collection whitelist for their own type, excluding same-ID parents from other collections.
A saved cursor no longer skips recovery when the list/detail page was never actually loaded; only projections carrying real load markers may be reused.
Sub-block removal or discard invalidates the list summary scope so a stale preview is not retained.
A sub-block added to an unrelated root no longer invalidates the open detail scope; a sub-block of the same root still does.
Moving a nested item from the annotation drift area to trash also cancels tasks bound to drift entries, matching mark cancellation.
Trend narrative rows and citation sources are allocated newest-first, so budget trimming drops the oldest dates and always retains the newest day.

A historical supplement that has waited across a local day receives the next available slot; same-day daily work and a failed daily repair stay ahead, so the supplement advances without starving current summaries.
The optional-prefixed /var/lib/for-now path no longer blocks the journal collector unit with 226/NAMESPACE at start.
